novelty_flags.label: thm:point-identification gap
novelty_flags.one_line: The gap says the source uses a conditional-support sufficient condition, but its published Assumption 4 is only marginal quasi-stayer support; the proof silently invokes the stronger conditional positivity.

soundness_flags.label: ass:continuous-regression
soundness_flags.one_line: Global \(g\in C(H)\) is tagged as a standard source condition, but the cited proceedings paper states continuity only at \((d_1,0)\) in its proof and does not assume a globally continuous regression on arbitrary \(H\).

soundness_flags.label: ass:static-schedules and def:legal-completion-class
soundness_flags.one_line: The condition uses undeclared two-argument schedules \(Y_t^Q(d_1,d_2)\), although the symbol table declares only \(Y_t^Q(d)\); declare the two-argument primitive or state static schedules directly with the declared schedule.

soundness_flags.label: thm:clipping-stability
soundness_flags.one_line: “Every observed cone is relaxed outward by \(\varepsilon\)” and the corresponding relaxed feasible class are not defined, so the clipping claim and sharp constant have no determinate domain.

soundness_flags.label: thm:finite-program and oeq:uniform-band-to-program
soundness_flags.one_line: Neither \(\mathcal C_{P,h}\) nor \(e_h\) is formally constructed, and the prose finite-program description does not specify its inner/outer feasible sets or objective approximation, leaving the Hausdorff and stochastic-program assertions undefined.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:honest-outer-ci
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Uniform coverage is conditional on an affirmative construction in oeq:uniform-band-to-program; this is honestly disclosed rather than presented as already derived.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The outer confidence-interval theorem is a conditional propagation result, valid under the stated regular subclass once the named band-to-program construction is supplied.

source_verification_receipts.version: AEA Papers and Proceedings 114 (2024), pp. 610–613, exact proceedings PDF
source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 611, Assumption 4; p. 613, proof of Theorem 1, especially the assertion following equation (3)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 4 states only \(P(\Delta D=0)=0\) and \(P(|\Delta D|\le\eta)>0\) for every \(η>0\), whereas the proof asserts \(P(|\Delta D|\le\eta\mid D_1)>0\) to define the conditional expectation. The paper also says only that \(g(d_1,\delta)\) is well defined and continuous at \((d_1,0)\).
For the common-zero-baseline heterogeneous-adoption design, Assumption 4 bounds conditional average slopes and Theorem 4 gives sharp WAS bounds, expressed as intersection bounds.
The paper treats finitely supported discrete \(X,W\), obtains sharp identified bounds from finite linear programs, and explicitly places continuously distributed variables outside its scope.

u_P\) uncertainty is propagated; then retain the displayed rate only for that concrete construction.
